scope: Central Front, northern face of the salient. All aviation divisions in the 16th Air Army row.
locator: Combat Composition of the Soviet Army, part III, 1 July 1943, Central Front, 16th Air Army row and front subtotal.
source_class: Soviet General Staff, postwar monthly combat-composition tables
interpretation: Six fighter, two assault, three bomber and one night-bomber division. The 5 July Central Front counterattack order confirms the army's task. Individual mission and airfield assignments require separate records.

scope: Voronezh Front, southern face of the salient. All aviation divisions in the 2nd Air Army row.
locator: Combat Composition of the Soviet Army, part III, 1 July 1943, Voronezh Front, 2nd Air Army row and front subtotal.
source_class: Soviet General Staff, postwar monthly combat-composition tables
interpretation: Five fighter, three assault, two bomber and one night-bomber division. The army contributed to the opening airfield strikes on 5 July. This roster establishes its composition four days earlier.

scope: Southwestern Front. All aviation divisions in the army that contributed to the 5 July airfield strikes alongside the 2nd Air Army.
locator: Combat Composition of the Soviet Army, part III, 1 July 1943, Southwestern Front, 17th Air Army row.
source_class: Soviet General Staff, postwar monthly combat-composition tables
interpretation: The nine divisions show the strength of the adjacent command in formations. The strike account identifies joint army participation. The detachment furnished by each division remains unresolved.

scope: Six squadrons listed for the Hungarian 2nd Air Brigade under VIII. Fliegerkorps in the Kharkov area.
locator: Newton, Kursk: The German View, Appendix 6A, Luftflotte Four, 1 July 1943, Hungarian brigade on p. 199.
interpretation: Two fighter squadrons and four reconnaissance, bombing and dive-bombing squadrons. The location applies to the brigade. Squadron designations follow the appendix.

scope: Numbered day-fighter Gruppen under Jagdabschnittführer Nr. 6.
locator: Order of Battle, 26 June 1944, Luftflotte 6, Jagdabschnittführer Nr. 6.
interpretation: Holm corroborates Mogilev for IV./JG 51 and Dokudovo for III./JG 11. The sources disagree on I./JG 51's station and on III./JG 11's aircraft type. The table gives no strength for IV./JG 51 or III./JG 11.

scope: Numbered assault Gruppen in the 1. and 4. Fliegerdivision sections.
locator: Order of Battle, 26 June 1944, Luftflotte 6, 1. Fliegerdivision and 4. Fliegerdivision.
interpretation: Two Gruppen appear under 1. Fliegerdivision and three under 4. Fliegerdivision. The source also names wing staffs and anti-tank Staffeln at different echelons.

scope: Numbered bomber Gruppen in the IV. Fliegerkorps section.
locator: Order of Battle, 26 June 1944, Luftflotte 6, IV. Fliegerkorps.
interpretation: Ten numbered Gruppen from KG 4, 27, 53 and 55. The same source lists II./KG 1 separately under Luftflotte 6 at Prohwehren. A station listing cannot establish a Gruppe's target or sortie.

scope: Fighter divisions explicitly named in the evening order for the encircled German force southeast of Bobruisk.
locator: 16th Air Army unit history, chapter 3, 27 June operational order, pp. 171–174 and note 14.
source_class: wartime operational order quoted in Soviet unit history
interpretation: All three divisions were ordered to protect bombers and assault aircraft by patrolling the edge of the encirclement. The army reported 134 fighters for the evening strike, without a division-by-division breakdown.

scope: Named examples of daytime regimental action in the account of the fighting for Bobruisk on 27 June.
locator: 16th Air Army unit history, chapter 3, 27 June, pp. 170–172, Titovka road column and Berezina bridge.
interpretation: The 569th attacked a road column and the 24th sent bombers against the bridge. These two examples give a lower bound. Published damage claims still need independent confirmation.

scope: 1st Baltic Front. All divisions in the 3rd Air Army row of the monthly combat-composition table.
locator: Combat Composition of the Soviet Army, part IV, 1 July 1944, 1st Baltic Front, 3rd Air Army row.
source_class: Soviet General Staff, postwar monthly combat-composition tables
interpretation: Seven divisions form the divisional roster. The army also had separate regiments, including the 6th Guards Assault Aviation Regiment. A claim about participation at Polotsk needs a dated operation record.

scope: 3rd Belorussian Front. All divisions in the 1st Air Army row of the monthly combat-composition table.
locator: Combat Composition of the Soviet Army, part IV, 1 July 1944, 3rd Belorussian Front, 1st Air Army row.
source_class: Soviet General Staff, postwar monthly combat-composition tables
interpretation: Eighteen divisions include the 303rd Fighter Aviation Division, the parent of the French Normandie regiment. The French journal supplies dated evidence of its own operations.

scope: 2nd Belorussian Front. All divisions in the 4th Air Army row of the monthly combat-composition table.
locator: Combat Composition of the Soviet Army, part IV, 1 July 1944, 2nd Belorussian Front, 4th Air Army row.
source_class: Soviet General Staff, postwar monthly combat-composition tables
interpretation: The five divisions accompanied separate reconnaissance, artillery-adjustment and communications aviation regiments. A dated list of their stations during the Mogilev advance remains open.

scope: 1st Belorussian Front. All divisions in the 6th Air Army row of the monthly combat-composition table.
locator: Combat Composition of the Soviet Army, part IV, 1 July 1944, 1st Belorussian Front, 6th Air Army row.
source_class: Soviet General Staff, postwar monthly combat-composition tables
interpretation: The monthly table lists three divisions under the army on the front's left wing. Its Lublin–Brest role developed later in July. This assignment cannot establish participation at Bobruisk.

scope: 1st Belorussian Front. All divisions in the 16th Air Army row of the monthly combat-composition table.
locator: Combat Composition of the Soviet Army, part IV, 1 July 1944, 1st Belorussian Front, 16th Air Army row.
source_class: Soviet General Staff, postwar monthly combat-composition tables
interpretation: Nineteen divisions under the front's right-wing air army. Three of its fighter divisions also occur in the separate 27 June Bobruisk order. The July roster cannot establish where every regiment flew in June.

scope: Aviation regiments in the Polish 1st Army row under the 1st Belorussian Front.
locator: Combat Composition of the Soviet Army, part IV, 1 July 1944, 1st Belorussian Front, 1st Army (Polish Army), aviation column.
source_class: Soviet General Staff, postwar monthly combat-composition tables
interpretation: Both regiments are listed under the Polish 1st Army. A Polish account dates the bombers' combat debut to 20 August and the fighters' to 23 August. See the eastern roster audit for the Warsaw-area evidence.

scope: Numbered German bomber, dive-bomber and assault Gruppen named under VIII. Fliegerkorps, southern sector.
locator: Newton, Kursk: The German View, Appendix 6A, Luftflotte Four, 1 July 1943, pp. 197–199.
interpretation: Five bomber, six dive-bomber and two assault Gruppen appear by number. KG 100 is a wing-level entry. Detached anti-tank Staffeln and the northern command require separate treatment.
